outcome: Clinical success rate (resolution of symptoms like heavy menstrual bleeding, iron-deficiency anemia, pelvic pressure)
cohort: 398 female patients under the age of 43 years who underwent uterine artery embolization between 2003 and 2017 for symptomatic fibroids and/or adenomyosis.
finding: The study found an overall clinical success rate of 91.2% with 109 live births out of 148 pregnancies, identifying restoration of uterine anatomy and ovarian protection as main predictive factors for obstetrical success.
birth_weight: Mean birthweight within normal limits (including preterm births)
gest_age: Average 35.12 ± 2.78 weeks for preterm births; 74 children born at term
